questions.question: Motion is defined as change in:
questions.explanation: Motion is defined as the change in position of an object with respect to time and a reference point. Mass, temperature, and density do not define motion.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of distance is:
questions.explanation: The S.I. unit of distance and length is the metre (m). Second is time, kilogram is mass, newton is force.

questions.question: The S.I. unit of speed is:
questions.explanation: Speed is distance per unit time, so its S.I. unit is m/s (metres per second). m/s2 is acceleration, m is length, s is time.

questions.question: Which is a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Speed is a scalar because it has magnitude only. Displacement, velocity, and acceleration are vectors.

questions.question: Which is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Displacement is a vector because it has both magnitude and direction. Distance, speed, and time are scalars.

questions.question: The rate of change of distance with time is:
questions.explanation: Speed is the rate of change of distance with time. Acceleration is rate of change of velocity; velocity is rate of change of displacement.

questions.question: The rate of change of displacement with time is:
questions.explanation: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time. It is a vector quantity.

questions.question: The rate of change of velocity with time is:
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.

questions.question: If a body moves with uniform velocity, its acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Uniform velocity means velocity is constant, so the rate of change of velocity is zero. Hence acceleration is zero.

questions.question: A body starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s<sup>2</sup> for 5 s. Its final velocity is:
questions.explanation: Using v = u + at, with u = 0, a = 2 m/s2, t = 5 s: v = 0 + 2 × 5 = 10 m/s.

questions.question: A car moving at 20 m/s decelerates uniformly at 4 m/s<sup>2</sup>. The time to stop is:
questions.explanation: Using v = u + at, with v = 0, u = 20 m/s, a = -4 m/s2: 0 = 20 - 4t, so 4t = 20, t = 5 s.

questions.question: The equation v = u + at relates:
options: Velocity, initial velocity, acceleration and time
questions.explanation: The equation v = u + at relates final velocity v, initial velocity u, acceleration a, and time t.

questions.question: The equation s = ut + ½at<sup>2</sup> is used when:
questions.explanation: The equation s = ut + ½at2 applies when acceleration is uniform (constant).

questions.question: The equation v<sup>2</sup> = u<sup>2</sup> + 2as relates:
options: Velocity, initial velocity, acceleration and displacement
questions.explanation: The equation v2 = u2 + 2as relates final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and displacement.

questions.question: A body moving with initial velocity 5 m/s accelerates at 3 m/s<sup>2</sup> for 4 s. The distance covered is:
questions.explanation: Using s = ut + ½at2: s = 5×4 + ½×3×42 = 20 + 24 = 44 m.

questions.question: The slope of a distance-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: The slope of a distance-time graph gives speed. Slope = change in distance / change in time.

questions.question: The slope of a velocity-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: The slope of a velocity-time graph gives acceleration. Slope = change in velocity / change in time.

questions.question: The area under a velocity-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: The area under a velocity-time graph gives the distance (or displacement) covered.

questions.question: In a distance-time graph, a horizontal line indicates:
questions.explanation: A horizontal line on a distance-time graph means distance is not changing with time, so the body is at rest.

questions.question: In a velocity-time graph, a horizontal line indicates:
questions.explanation: A horizontal line on a velocity-time graph means velocity is constant, so the body moves with constant velocity.

questions.question: Acceleration due to gravity on earth is approximately:
questions.explanation: The acceleration due to gravity on Earth is approximately 9.8 m/s2.

questions.question: A stone is dropped from rest. Its velocity after 3 s is [g = 10 m/s<sup>2</sup>]:
questions.explanation: Using v = u + gt, with u = 0, g = 10 m/s2, t = 3 s: v = 0 + 10×3 = 30 m/s.

questions.question: A body falls freely from rest for 4 s. The distance fallen is [g = 10 m/s<sup>2</sup>]:
questions.explanation: Using s = ut + ½gt2, with u = 0: s = ½×10×42 = 5×16 = 80 m.

questions.question: The time of flight of a projectile projected at angle θ with initial velocity u is:
questions.explanation: The time of flight for a projectile is T = 2u sin θ / g.

questions.question: The maximum height of a projectile is:
questions.explanation: The maximum height of a projectile is H = u2 sin2 θ / (2g).

questions.question: The horizontal range of a projectile is maximum when the angle of projection is:
questions.explanation: The horizontal range is maximum when the angle of projection is 45°, giving R = u2/g.

questions.question: A projectile has maximum range when projected at:
questions.explanation: Maximum range occurs at 45° for a projectile on level ground.

questions.question: The centripetal acceleration of a body moving in a circle of radius r with speed v is:
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration is a = v2/r, directed towards the centre of the circle.

questions.question: The angular velocity of a body in circular motion is given by:
questions.explanation: Angular velocity ω = v/r, where v is linear speed and r is radius.

questions.question: The period of a body in circular motion of radius r and speed v is:
questions.explanation: Period T = circumference / speed = 2πr/v.

questions.question: Relative velocity of two bodies moving in opposite directions with speeds v<sub>1</sub> and v<sub>2</sub> is:
questions.explanation: For opposite directions, relative velocity is the sum of speeds: v1 + v2.

questions.question: Relative velocity of two bodies moving in same direction with speeds v<sub>1</sub> and v<sub>2</sub> (v<sub>1</sub> > v<sub>2</sub>) is:
questions.explanation: For same direction, relative velocity is the difference of speeds: v1 − v2.

questions.question: Newton's first law of motion is also called the law of:
questions.explanation: Newton's first law is also called the law of inertia, because it describes the tendency of a body to resist changes in its state of motion.

questions.question: Newton's second law of motion states that force is equal to:
questions.explanation: Newton's second law: F = ma, force equals mass times acceleration.

questions.question: Newton's third law of motion states that action and reaction are:
options: Equal and in the same direction
questions.explanation: Newton's third law: for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

questions.question: The momentum of a body of mass m moving with velocity v is:
questions.explanation: Momentum p = mv, the product of mass and velocity.

questions.question: Impulse is equal to:
questions.explanation: Impulse = force × time = change in momentum.

questions.question: A body of mass 2 kg moving at 5 m/s has momentum:
questions.explanation: Momentum p = mv = 2 × 5 = 10 kg m/s.

questions.question: A force of 10 N acts on a mass of 2 kg. The acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Using F = ma, a = F/m = 10/2 = 5 m/s2.

questions.question: A body moving with uniform acceleration covers 100 m in 5 s. If initial velocity is zero, acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Using s = ut + ½at2, with u = 0: 100 = ½ × a × 52 = 12.5a, so a = 100/12.5 = 8 m/s2.

questions.question: A car accelerates uniformly from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 5 s. Its acceleration is:
The distance covered by a body moving at constant speed 15 m/s for 8 s is:
questions.explanation: Distance = speed × time = 15 × 8 = 120 m.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Speed is a scalar quantity. Acceleration, displacement, and force are vectors.

questions.question: A body moving in a circle at constant speed has:
questions.explanation: Although speed is constant, the direction of motion changes continuously, so velocity is changing.

questions.question: The acceleration of a body in circular motion is directed:
questions.explanation: The centripetal acceleration is directed towards the centre of the circular path.

questions.question: A particle moves 3 m east then 4 m north. Its displacement is:
questions.explanation: Displacement is the straight-line distance from start to finish: √(32 + 42) = √25 = 5 m.

questions.question: A particle moves 3 m east then 4 m north. The total distance covered is:
questions.explanation: Total distance is the sum of path lengths: 3 + 4 = 7 m.

questions.question: The area under an acceleration-time graph gives:
questions.explanation: The area under an acceleration-time graph gives the change in velocity.

questions.question: A body thrown vertically upwards with velocity u reaches maximum height h. The time to reach maximum height is:
questions.explanation: At maximum height, v = 0. Using v = u - gt: 0 = u - gt, so t = u/g.

questions.question: A body is projected vertically upwards with 20 m/s. The maximum height reached is [g = 10 m/s<sup>2</sup>]:
questions.explanation: Using v2 = u2 - 2gh, with v = 0: 0 = 202 - 2×10×h, so 400 = 20h, h = 20 m.
